developer_request: This long-running product repository has old deployment records, release notes, and many prior AI edits. Understand the current state and continue the product work.
known_facts: The root project instructions declare a short mandatory first-read order containing current project status, current product contract, and current implementation state.
The same instructions explicitly say historical release/deployment/server records are not current sources unless the task specifically concerns history or future release re-authorization.
The repository's branch name and historical files can misleadingly suggest an active production state even though the declared current-status source says otherwise.
The current product contract already narrows the highest-priority user journey before broad technical cleanup.
expected_first_moves: Follow the repository-declared first-read order before broad file/history search.
Use the declared current-status and product-contract sources to establish current stage and product priority.
Inspect only the code/tests relevant to the first current product path to be stabilized.
Open historical deployment/release evidence only if a concrete current question cannot be answered without it.
must_preserve: The repository owner's declared current-source hierarchy and explicit historical-source exclusions.
The distinction between branch/file history and current operational reality.
The current product-loop priority over broad cleanup or feature accumulation.
must_not: Infer active production merely from a production-named branch, release documents, or server records.
Read all historical deployment material before the declared current sources.
Treat a large repository as justification for exhaustive discovery before selecting the first current product path.
lessons: Explicit project read-order and exclusion rules are themselves discovery controls and should beat generic repository-wide scanning.
Brownfield recovery should reconstruct current truth from declared authority first, then inspect only the implementation surface needed for the next high-value path.
